newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico guerrilla group calls off armed struggle.
newsitem.headline: Mexico guerrilla group calls off armed struggle.

text.p: The leftist Mexican guerrilla group known as the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) said on Tuesday it would temporarily suspend offensive military operations to concentrate on a propaganda campaign.

"We have decided not to attack, in the course of this campaign, either police or military positions, reserving the right to repel with arms any governmental aggression," the EPR said in a statement received in the southern city of Oaxaca.
The EPR unveiled itself in the southwestern state of Guerrero on June 28 during a ceremony marking the anniversary of a state police massacre of 17 peasants.
Since then it has launched attacks in several Mexican states, including against military installations just outside the capital of Mexico City. About 25 people have been killed and nearly 50 injured.
The EPR is unrelated to the Maya Indian-based Zapatista guerrilla movement in the southeastern state of Chiapas. The Zapatistas and the government are nearing a peace agreement.
The latest EPR statement, dated Monday and made available to Reuters late on Tuesday, was signed by the "General Command" of the guerrilla group.
It criticised government corruption and the unequal distribution of wealth in Mexico, calling for "a country where big capital serves the workers with an aim toward resolving their needs."
Backtracking from its previous stated goal of seeking a direct road to power through arms, the EPR said it would concentrate on a propaganda campaign.
"In the framework of this campaign, we have decided to transmit our proposals and our political ideas through armed revolutionary propaganda," the statement said.
Although there is no troop count for the EPR, military experts do not rate it as a serious threat to the Mexican army.
